cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Outsmart the Room
cards.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put 'butler' above your answer on the murder-mystery board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We both said butler at the same time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Simultaneous guesses aren't deductions. List your evidence; I'll put it in order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The muddy shoes. Same evidence you used.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine is written as a deduction. Yours is just 'butler'. Add the shoes underneath, and leave my answer at the top.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects B2 equal guesses as deficient method and A5 tries to rank identical evidence, keeping the contest active.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 simultaneous answer leads A3 evidence demand; B4 same evidence leads A5 writing distinction, but that distinction needs board content not previously established.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 object reasonably to A claiming superiority from shared answer and clue.

heightening.evidence: A5 changes the criterion after B4 equalizes the evidence, a causal contest development.

specificity.evidence: A1 names a murder mystery and butler answer; B4 supplies muddy shoes. A5 suddenly claims A's writing is a fuller deduction, not established by A1.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 has a concrete writing request, but its preceding claim depends on an ambiguous unseen difference.

coach2.situation: A1 names a murder mystery and butler answer; B4 supplies muddy shoes. A5 suddenly claims A's writing is a fuller deduction, not established by A1.
coach2.stated: A1 wrote butler above B's answer; B2 both said it together; B4 both used muddy shoes; A5 claims fuller written deduction.
coach2.inferred: A wants the board to rank A above B, not merely report the solution.
coach2.missing: The difference in written reasoning is not established; do not assume staging supplies it.
coach2.firstDefect: A5's claimed written superiority needs either an explicit earlier fact or removal.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 objects to the ranking A1 creates for identical answers.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 treats B2 simultaneous response as a reason to demand evidence.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 supplies shared evidence in response to A3.

B4-A5.evidence: UNCLEAR: A5 claims different written forms after B4 equal evidence, but A1 only establishes butler written above another answer.

format.evidence: A1, B2, A3, B4 and A5 satisfy the unchanged ABABA structure and 125-word pair limit.

reservation: Repair A5 to direct where B's already-established clue goes rather than invent a visible difference in the earlier writing.
provenance: Explicit direct assistant assessment/rereading; not fresh, independent, human, or worker proof.
